searchText: Question, EIP-2780 doesn't state what if the gas budget is insufficient for charging the account-creation if the recipient is empty and transaction carries value; or the charge for accessing delegate; This must be processed after applying the authorization, therefore, not part of IntrinsicCost. My question is, if gas is not enough, shall we invalidate the entire the transaction as we do in other cases (before entering the call frame)? Or we just interpret it as an exceptional halt. If the transaction OOGs here, I believe it is to be interpreted as an Exceptional halt. I remember this was part of the EIP text at one point but might have been deleted by accident. <@968526635735326741> I think it might be worth adding back the OOG scenario explicitly in this [line](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/34f7405965ea5cc7135050e1741d903971a1fb6b/EIPS/eip-2780.md?plain=1#L85), along with contract creating tx initcode revert. The whole idea behind splitting the gas charges into intrinsic gas + later charge for new account creation/ delegation access, was to allow transactions to be validated/invalidated without needing further state access Agreed. I will update the EIP For confirmation, spec (and tests) are still doing eip7702 refund to the reservoir, and not doing source based refund, right? For confirmation, spec (and tests) are I have a question why the access list doesn't worm the 7702 delegations? See test `test_top_frame_charges_delegation_in_access_list`. The delegation is in the access list, but the top level frame continues to charge cold access cost. See [here](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/34f7405965ea5cc7135050e1741d903971a1fb6b/EIPS/eip-2780.md?plain=1#L80) More context here https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1504670887851327648/1509909296471736472 It seems we are stacking up exceptions to the exceptions... and the EIP is not consistent. https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3045 But at least we make it very hard for zkEVM to catch up... very well. For me this is horrible change. I have a warm account (because access list says so) and suddenly during EVM execution in one place how am I suppose to know if an account was warmed by access list or some other rule?
